channel.title: saltco — Open-Source Computing & Capacity Building
channel.description: Open-source geospatial AI education. Learn GIS, Python, and AI with tools that run offline.

item.title: Applied Spatial Analysis Using QGIS - Capstone Briefing & Final Session
item.description: Session 9 of 9, the final briefing: one capstone project worth 260 points and 52% of the course. The six graded components and weights, the Sudan data and its limits, six project options, the submission folder, the six defence questions, and the three-month window to the hard deadline of 7 February 2027.

item.title: Applied Spatial Analysis Using QGIS - Low-Bandwidth Offline Web Maps
item.description: Week 8 (Project 5B): join the district population CSV to admin2_districts, calculate area and population density in the Field Calculator, style with five Natural Breaks classes, clean the popup aliases, then export a qgis2web/Leaflet folder that opens offline in any browser — no QGIS, no install. Plus the two failures from our own export: a virtual join that lost the population column, and a basemap that only existed on localhost.

item.title: Applied Spatial Analysis Using QGIS - Professional Print Layouts & Atlas
item.description: Week 7 (Project 5A): turn analysis into a printable map with guides, main map and inset, grid, legend, scale bar and north arrow, then use the QGIS Atlas with states intersecting a 5 km railway buffer to generate one 300 DPI sheet per state.

item.title: Applied Spatial Analysis Using QGIS - Raster Analysis & Demographic Planning
item.description: Week 6 (Project 4B): pixels to decisions. Reproject the DEM to UTM 36N, clip it to Red Sea state, derive slope and aspect, turn site criteria into a boolean raster with the Raster Calculator, then raster to vector, a dissolved 5 km railway buffer, and an intersection that leaves the best sites over 150 acres.

item.title: Applied Spatial Analysis Using QGIS - Spatial Proximity & Multi-Criteria Analysis
item.description: Week 5 (Project 4A): Study Area → Clip → Buffer → Spatial Join. Data prep first, filter main roads with expressions, run 30 m/100 m buffers, then use Spatial Join to find impacted vs unimpacted buildings in metres (UTM 36N).

item.title: Applied Spatial Analysis Using QGIS - Attribute Queries, Expressions & Selection Math
item.description: Week 4 (Project 3): why the attribute table is the real dataset behind the map — sorting, field types, the Field Calculator, styling by attribute, the Expression Builder, and the CASE WHEN mistake that costs everyone an hour.

item.title: Applied Spatial Analysis Using QGIS - Cadastral Boundary Mapping & Topology
item.description: Week 3 (Project 2): cadastral vs topographic — the difference is the intent of the map, not its subject matter. Then the Attribute Form, snapping set up before digitizing, neighbouring parcels sharing one boundary, and a clean Topology Checker run with no gaps and no overlaps in EPSG:32636.

item.title: Applied Spatial Analysis Using QGIS - Permanent Metric Transformation
item.description: Week 2 (Project 1B): create data from scratch — a LineString and a parks polygon layer digitized in QGIS — then permanently reproject from WGS84 to UTM Zone 36N (EPSG:32636) and compute real areas in square metres with the Field Calculator and $area.

item.title: Applied Spatial Analysis Using QGIS - Field Data Import & Contextualization
item.description: Week 1 (Project 1A): the standard GIS project folder structure, a first tour of the QGIS interface, importing a CSV of field points as real features, symbolising, exporting to GeoPackage — and a GPX track for contrast.

item.title: Applied Spatial Analysis Using QGIS - Orientation & GIS Literacy
item.description: Applied Spatial Analysis Using QGIS - Orientation & GIS Literacy: GIS defined, spatial vs aspatial, vector vs raster, why 70% is data cleaning, framing a fundable GIS proposal, and configuring QGIS for UTM 36N.

item.title: It Starts at the Keyboard: Why I Teach Open Source from the Bottom Up
item.description: From teaching high school finals on my vacations to carrying 8TB of open source knowledge to Sudan — the department that could not save its own letters, and why I start every learner at the basics.

item.title: One Route, Two Branches: The Training Route Map
item.description: From the typing gate and Linux foundation to LibreOffice, GIS & QGIS, Python, PyQGIS, and AI for geospatial analytics — the whole journey on two pages.

item.title: Don't Throw It Away — How Linux Gives Old Laptops a Second Life
item.description: An old laptop is not obsolete — it's just running the wrong software. Why Linux revives old hardware and makes powerful, free computing possible for everyone.

item.title: How Linux and Open Source Enhanced My Computing Skills
item.description: My journey from proprietary GIS software to Linux and open source — and why I now teach it to people with limited resources.
